stories.headline: National Revolution and Solidarity Day observed on 7 November
stories.summary: Bangladesh observes National Revolution and Solidarity Day as a public holiday. The 2026 observance marks the 51st anniversary of the events of 7 November 1975. TBS reports that soldiers freed then army chief Major General Ziaur Rahman from house arrest at Dhaka Cantonment after the 3 November 1975 coup led by Brigadier Khaled Mosharraf.
stories.why_it_matters: A recurring national observance with high relevance to Bangladesh history, political development and state commemorations.
stories.exam_facts: 7 November is observed as National Revolution and Solidarity Day; the 2026 observance is the 51st anniversary; Ziaur Rahman was then army chief and was released from house arrest.
stories.key_people: Government of Bangladesh; Major General Ziaur Rahman; Brigadier Khaled Mosharraf; BNP; Dhaka Cantonment.
stories.figures: 51st anniversary in 2026; historical sequence includes the 3 November 1975 coup and 7 November 1975 uprising.

stories.headline: Business approval reform aims to reduce startup clearance time from 355 days to 18
stories.summary: A committee reviewing industrial setup procedures discussed an Invest Bangladesh roadmap to reduce the time for business licences, clearances and approvals from as much as 355 days to an interim 18 days. The government's ultimate target is 14 days. The plan includes processing 11 of 12 statutory documents within one day each, fewer prerequisites, parallel processing and a single digital platform.
stories.why_it_matters: Reducing administrative delays can improve the investment climate, encourage domestic and foreign investment and lower the cost of starting a business.
stories.exam_facts: Interim target: 18 days; ultimate target: 14 days; the roadmap was presented by Invest Bangladesh.
stories.key_people: Invest Bangladesh; Commerce and Industries Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir; committee on industrial setup procedures.
stories.figures: 355 days current reported maximum; 18-day interim roadmap; 14-day ultimate target; 11 of 12 statutory documents targeted for one-day processing.

stories.headline: World Bank reports Bangladesh external debt at $113.44 billion in 2025
stories.event_date_note: World Bank International Debt Report 2026 released 2026-11-05; data reference year 2025
stories.summary: The World Bank's 2026 International Debt Statistics table records Bangladesh's total external debt stock at US$113.4378 billion in 2025, up from US$104.4951 billion in 2024, an increase of about 8.6%. The official table gives long-term public and publicly guaranteed (PPG) external debt of US$83.4567 billion, external debt-to-GNI of 23.6% and debt service-to-exports of 15.7%.
stories.why_it_matters: External debt affects debt sustainability, foreign-exchange management, budget choices and the country's capacity to finance development.
stories.exam_facts: The official World Bank table gives total external debt of US$113.4bn in 2025; debt/GNI 23.6%; debt service/exports 15.7%.
stories.key_people: World Bank Group; International Development Association (IDA); Asian Development Bank (ADB); Bangladesh government and borrowers.
stories.figures: Total external debt: US$113.4378bn in 2025; 2024: US$104.4951bn; long-term PPG debt: US$83.4567bn; debt/GNI: 23.6%; debt service/exports: 15.7%.

stories.headline: BSEC seeks five-year extension and larger size for banks' capital-market funds
stories.event_date_note: BSEC letter dated 2026-10-29; existing facility expires 2026-12-31
stories.summary: BSEC asked Bangladesh Bank to extend banks' special capital-market investment funds for five years from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2031 and raise the maximum fund size from Tk200 crore to Tk300 crore per scheduled bank. stories.headline: Islami Bank proposes to raise authorised capital fivefold to Tk10,000 crore
stories.summary: Islami Bank Bangladesh's board proposed increasing authorised capital from Tk2,000 crore to Tk10,000 crore. The proposal requires amendments to the bank's Memorandum and Articles of Association and approval from Bangladesh Bank, other regulators and shareholders at an Extraordinary General Meeting. The bank reported a July-September 2026 loss of Tk1,970 crore, compared with a Tk32 crore profit in the same quarter of 2025.
stories.why_it_matters: The proposal highlights bank capital adequacy, asset quality, governance, non-performing investments and the difference between authorised and paid-up capital.
stories.exam_facts: Proposed increase: Tk2,000 crore to Tk10,000 crore; the proposal is not effective until regulatory and shareholder approvals are obtained.

stories.figures: Proposed authorised capital: Tk10,000 crore, up from Tk2,000 crore; Q3 loss: Tk1,970 crore; prior-year Q3 profit: Tk32 crore; loss per share: Tk12.24.

stories.headline: Trust Bank joins Bangladesh Bank's Tk2,000 crore leather-sector pre-finance scheme
stories.summary: Trust Bank signed a participation agreement with Bangladesh Bank under the central bank's Tk2,000 crore pre-finance scheme for the leather industry. The scheme offers end-borrower financing at an annual interest rate of up to 7% and covers leather processing, tanneries, leather goods, footwear and related support industries.

stories.headline: BRAC Bank completes Bangladesh's first fully digital export documentary collection
stories.summary: BRAC Bank completed a fully digital export documentary collection using blockchain technology and an electronic bill of lading (eBL). stories.figures: Document processing: 40 days to 1 day. This refers to document processing only, not the full export shipment or payment cycle.

stories.headline: Bangladesh and Russia discuss long-term LNG/LPG supplies and alternative payment routes
stories.summary: The fifth Bangladesh-Russia Intergovernmental Commission meeting discussed possible long-term LNG and LPG supplies, including potential imports from Russia's Sakhalin-2 and Portovaya facilities. The talks also covered alternative payment mechanisms because sanctions have disrupted conventional banking channels. Bangladesh Bank data cited by the report show Bangladesh paid US$1.36 billion for imports from Russia in FY2025.

stories.headline: Tk4,068 crore Mongla Port expansion and modernisation project launched
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman laid the foundation stone of the Tk4,068 crore Mongla Port Expansion and Modernisation Project in Mongla, Bagerhat. The plan includes upgraded cargo and supply-chain facilities and improved road connectivity between Panchagarh and Mongla. Once completed, container trains are expected to run directly between Kamalapur Inland Container Depot in Dhaka and Mongla Port. A cooperation MoU with a Chinese firm was also reported.
stories.why_it_matters: Port capacity and inland connectivity can lower logistics costs, support exports and imports, and encourage more balanced regional development.

stories.key_people: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman; Mongla Port Authority; Government of Bangladesh; Chinese infrastructure partner; Bangladesh Railway.
stories.figures: Project cost: Tk4,068 crore; planned direct rail link: Kamalapur ICD to Mongla Port.

stories.headline: Government hopes to resume Malaysia-bound worker recruitment in December
stories.summary: Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said Bangladesh hopes to resume sending workers to Malaysia from December. He said the first two or three flights should carry workers free of charge; private-agency migration costs for others were estimated at Tk2.5 lakh to Tk3 lakh. The minister described an online application and lottery process and said a new MoU was expected on 31 December.
stories.why_it_matters: Malaysia is an important labour market for Bangladesh. Transparent recruitment and lower migration costs affect remittance earnings, worker protection and household debt.
stories.exam_facts: The minister expressed an expectation, not a guarantee; first two or three flights were proposed to be free; other costs were estimated at Tk2.5–3 lakh.
stories.key_people: Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury; Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment; recruiting agencies; Bangladesh and Malaysia.
stories.figures: Expected resumption: December 2026; first 2–3 flights proposed free; estimated private-agency cost: Tk2.5–3 lakh; proposed MoU date: 31 December.

stories.headline: COP31 to focus on implementation, fossil-fuel transition and climate finance; UNEP reports a large adaptation-finance gap
stories.summary: COP31 will take place in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026. Türkiye will host; Murat Kurum is nominated as conference president and Australia's Chris Bowen will preside over negotiations. Reuters reported that fossil-fuel phase-outs and climate finance are central issues. UNEP's 2026 Adaptation Gap Report estimates international public adaptation finance at US$28.2–31.7 billion in 2024, against developing-country needs of US$305 billion annually by 2035.
stories.why_it_matters: Climate finance and adaptation are especially important to vulnerable developing countries, including Bangladesh, which faces cyclones, floods, heat stress and sea-level rise.
stories.exam_facts: COP31 is in Antalya, Türkiye; conference dates are 9–20 November 2026; UNEP estimates US$305bn annual adaptation needs by 2035; 2024 public flows were US$28.2–31.7bn.
stories.key_people: UNFCCC; UNEP; Türkiye; Murat Kurum; Chris Bowen; Climate Analytics; developing-country negotiators.

stories.headline: China adopts law targeting cross-border corruption
stories.summary: Reuters reported, citing China's state news agency Xinhua, that China adopted a law targeting cross-border corruption. Reported provisions include stronger cooperation to track fugitives, prevent suspects from fleeing abroad, recover illicit assets, protect state and commercial secrets and personal data, and require Chinese companies engaged in cross-border business to establish anti-corruption compliance functions proportionate to their risks.
stories.why_it_matters: The law expands anti-corruption enforcement beyond national borders and has implications for international legal cooperation, asset recovery and corporate compliance.
stories.exam_facts: China adopted a law targeting cross-border corruption; reported aims include fugitive tracking and illicit-asset recovery; corporate anti-corruption compliance duties are part of the reported framework.
stories.key_people: National People's Congress Standing Committee; Xinhua; President Xi Jinping; senior anti-corruption official Li Xi.
stories.figures: Law adopted 6 November 2026; draft first reviewed in August 2025, according to Reuters' account.

mcqs.question: The word 'bureaucratic' most nearly means:

options.B: Relating to administrative rules and procedures

mcqs.explanation: Bureaucratic describes administration through rules and procedures, often with excessive formality or delay.

mcqs.question: Choose the closest synonym of 'overhaul' in the context of reforming a system:
mcqs.explanation: To overhaul a system is to examine and restructure it thoroughly; revamp is the closest option.

mcqs.question: 'Statutory documents' are documents that are:
mcqs.explanation: Statutory means created, required or regulated by law.

mcqs.question: A 'prerequisite' is:

options.A: A condition that must be met beforehand

mcqs.explanation: A prerequisite is a precondition or requirement that must be satisfied first.

mcqs.question: Which word is closest to the opposite of 'streamline'?
mcqs.explanation: To streamline is to make a process simpler and more efficient; complicate is the opposite.

mcqs.question: In banking, 'liquidity' refers mainly to:

options.A: The legal ownership of a bank
options.B: The total number of bank branches
options.C: The age of a loan officer
options.D: The availability of cash or readily convertible assets

mcqs.explanation: Liquidity is the ability to meet payments using cash or assets that can be converted into cash quickly.

mcqs.question: Which expression is the best opposite of a 'blanket extension'?
mcqs.explanation: A blanket extension applies generally; a case-by-case extension is selective and individually assessed.

mcqs.question: 'Bilateral trade' is trade:

options.B: Among every country in the world

mcqs.explanation: Bilateral means involving two parties, commonly two countries.

mcqs.question: In the phrase 'sanctions-related barriers', 'sanctions' means:
mcqs.explanation: Economic sanctions are official restrictions or penalties imposed on a country, entity or person.

mcqs.question: Choose the closest synonym of 'facilitate':
mcqs.explanation: Facilitate means to make something easier; enable is the closest synonym.

mcqs.question: 'Free of charge' means:
mcqs.explanation: The fixed phrase means that no payment is required.

mcqs.question: To 'phase out fossil fuels' means to:
mcqs.explanation: The phrasal verb phase out means to remove or discontinue something gradually.

mcqs.question: What is the interim business-approval timeline in the Invest Bangladesh roadmap reported on 6 November?
